podcast.title: Early Career with The Box Tops (1967)
podcast.body: As a 16-year-old, Alex Chilton served as the lead singer for The Box Tops, achieving a smash single with "The Letter" in the summer of 1967. After The Box Tops disbanded, Chilton went on to form Big Star. "Their frontman was Alex Chilton, who as a 16 year old kid, was the lead singer for the box tops on their summer of 67 Smash single The Letter."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Commercial Flop, Critical Success
xref.body: Big Star, with frontman Alex Chilton, aimed to follow in the footsteps of The Beatles and The Kinks while also admiring The Beach Boys' melodies. Despite being major critical darlings with a strong following among other musicians, they struggled with a bad record deal, failed to achieve hit singles, and sold few records, leading to their breakup after three years. "Unfortunately for Big Star, they couldn't manage any hit singles and never sold many records."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Reunion and Alex Chilton's Death
xref.body: The band reunited in 1993 and remained active until singer Alex Chilton passed away from a heart attack, marking the end of their second phase. "A cult following built, and in 1993, the group reunited and stayed together until singer Alex Chilton died of a heart attack."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
